question: In the context of crust, the main mineral constituents of the continental mass are _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**silica and alumina**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Earth's crust** is the uppermost layer over the Earth's surface. It is the thinnest of all the layers, making up only about **1%** of the Earth's total volume.
 
• The **continental mass** of the crust is primarily composed of **silica** and **alumina**. Because of these two main mineral constituents, it is frequently referred to as **sial** (**si** for silica and **al** for alumina).
 
• The **thickness** of the crust varies significantly between the landmasses and the ocean floor. On the **continental masses**, the thickness is approximately **35 km**.
